decision_conditions:
Materials 



No above ground development
shall commence on each relevant block until full details, including samples,
specifications and annotated plans of all external facing materials have been
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. On-site
sample panels shall be provided for officer inspection where requested. The
development shall only be implemented in accordance with the approved details
and to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority and shall be retained
in perpetuity thereafter.

Soft Landscaping 



The planting scheme for the development shown on the plans
hereby approved shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons
following the first occupation or the completion of the relevant part of the
development, whichever is the sooner. Any trees or plants which within a period
of 5 years from the completion of the entire development die, are removed or
become seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting
season with others of similar size and species unless the Local Planning
Authority gives written consent to any variation. The planting scheme shall be maintained
thereafter.

Hard Landscaping



The hard landscaping scheme hereby
approved shall be implemented prior to first occupation of the relevant part of
the development and shall thereafter be permanently maintained to the
satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.

Children’s Play Spacea)    Notwithstanding the details shown on the drawings
hereby approved, prior to commencement of the construction of play areas,
details of the children's play spaces including all proposed equipment, associated
landscaping and implementation strategy shall be submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority.







b)    Prior to occupation of the relevant part of the
development, or otherwise in accordance with the implementation strategy, the play
equipment shall be installed and thereafter maintained in perpetuity to the
satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.

Green Roof Systems



Prior to commencement of above ground works, details
of a maintenance plan of the green roof systems shall be submitted to, and
approved by, the Local Planning Authority. Once approved the maintenance plan
shall be implemented and thereafter permanently retained.

Cycle Parking



Notwithstanding the details shown on the plans hereby
approved, prior to commencement of the cycle parking facilities, details of the
cycle parking facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. The submission shall include details of the security,
monitoring and access arrangements for the cycle parking facilities. They shall
detail the provision of visitor cycle parking, the quantum and mix in each
store, and access arrangements to be via a core and/or residents’ communal
gardens. The development shall not be occupied until the approved details have
been implemented for the respective block. Thereafter, the cycle parking
facilities shall be retained in perpetuity.

Car Parking Management



Prior to occupation, a car
parking management and allocation strategy shall be submitted to and approved
in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This shall set out the management
and allocation strategy for the wheelchair accessible parking bays for the use
of any initial or future registered disabled occupiers of the development. It
shall also set out the management for visitor parking bays. The strategy shall
thereafter be maintained in perpetuity.

Delivery and Servicing
Plan



Prior to the first occupation of development, a
detailed Delivery and Servicing Plan (DSP) in line with Transport for London
(TfL) guidelines shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local
Planning Authority. The DSP should provide details of the expected type and
frequency of service vehicles including waste removal, the hours within which
they would arrive and depart, the intended locations for loading and unloading
of vehicles and associated waiting and turning areas and access routes and show
clear vehicle sweep paths based on up to date information in relation to
overall vehicle movements associated with the development. The relevant details
regarding shall be fully implemented prior to the first occupation of any
residential units and shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved
details in perpetuity.

Waste Management
Strategy



The waste management
provisions hereby approved in the Operational Waste Management Plan (ref: ‘85323
-CUR-00-XX-T-TP-00003_Rev.03’ prepared by Curtins, dated 16/06/2025) shall be
fully implemented prior to first occupation of the relevant block, and shall be
retained in perpetuity thereafter.

Housing Mix and Tenure



The development shall be
carried out in accordance with the housing mix and tenures specified in Table
2.1 of the Planning Statement of Compliance Rev. A by Savills dated August 2025,
and at 2.9 of the Design and Access Statement by GRID Architects dated
18/06/2025 and maintained for the lifetime of the development.

Accessible Units (M4(2)
and M4(3)) Ten percent (10%) of the
residential units hereby permitted shall be constructed to achieve Building
Regulations (2016) M4(3) 'Wheelchair user dwellings' standards.Ninety percent (90%) of the
residential units hereby permitted shall be constructed to achieve Building
Regulations (2016) M4(2) 'Accessible and adaptable dwellings' standards.

Microclimate Mitigation



Prior to occupation of the
relevant parts of the development, the wind mitigation measures outlined in the
Wind Microclimate CFD Study (ref: ‘WH532-01F03(rev2)’ prepared by Windtech
Consultants dated 12/06/2025) shall be implemented in full and shall thereafter
be retained in perpetuity.

Secured by Design



The proposed development
shall achieve Secured by Design certification to the satisfaction of the local
authority & Metropolitan Police, details of which shall be provided to the
Local Planning Authority for its written approval prior to the first occupation
of the approved development. All security measures applied to the approved
development shall be permanently retained thereafter.

Vents, Pipes, Shutters or Extracts



No vents, plumbing, pipes, external shutters, other utilities
equipment or similar, other than those shown on the drawings hereby approved,
shall be fixed to the external faces of the buildings, unless otherwise agreed
in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Non-Road Mobile
Machinery (NRMM)



No NRMM shall be used on the
site unless it is compliant with the NRMM Low Emission Zone requirements (or
any superseding requirements) and until it has been registered for use on the
site on the NRMM register (or any superseding register).

Noise Protection Scheme – External Noise Attenuation for
Noise-Sensitive Development The building envelope of the development to which the application
refers shall be constructed to provide sound attenuation against externally
generated noise sources to achieve the internal ambient noise levels detailed
in Table 1 below. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined
in accordance with the latest British Standard 8233:2014 ‘Guidance on sound
insulation and noise reduction for buildings’ and ‘Professional Practice
Guidance: Planning & Noise – New Residential Development’ (2017) (or
equivalent if replaced). No above ground development shall commence on each relevant block
until noise attenuation details have been submitted to the Local Planning
Authority (LPA) for approval in writing.  Any works which form part of the
scheme shall be completed in accordance with the approved details before the
dwellings are occupied and shall thereafter be retained as approved. Internal noise levels should be achieved with windows open for
rapid ventilation purposes. Where this cannot be achieved alternative means of
ventilation and cooling will be required. Where whole house ventilation is
provided then acoustically treated inlets and outlets should ideally be located
away from the façade(s) most exposed to noise (and any local sources of air
pollution). Any ventilation strategy shall consider the Association of Noise
Consultants ‘Acoustics, Ventilation and Overheating: Residential Design Guide’
(2020).

The design and layout of the development shall be constructed to
protect external amenity spaces (including gardens, balconies and terraces)
against externally Generated noise sources to achieve 50dB(A) LAeq,16hour
with a maximum limit of 55dB(A) LAeq,16hour. Any works which form
part of the scheme shall be completed in accordance with the approved details
before the dwellings are occupied and shall thereafter be retained as approved.
The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined in accordance with
the Professional Practice Guidance: Planning & Noise – New Residential
Development’ (2017) (or equivalent if replaced).

Noise Generating
Mechanical Services Plant Before any mechanical services
plant including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), to which the
application refers, is used at the premises, a scheme shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA) which demonstrates
that the following noise design requirements can be complied with and shall
thereafter be retained as approved. a)    The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of
noise emitted from the mechanical services plant to which the application
refers, shall be lower than the existing background noise level by 10dB at
all times when the plant is in operation. Measurements
shall be made at a height of 1.2 – 1.5 metres above the adjacent ground level
and at least 3.5 metres from any sound reflecting surfaces other than the
ground or 1 metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise
sensitive premises, and in accordance with the latest British Standard
BS4142:2014. The measurement value shall be adjusted to remove the additional
sound energy contribution from reflected surfaces other than from the ground. An
alternative position for assessment /measurement may be used to allow ease of
access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed
to show how the design criteria is achieved. b)    The plant shall be isolated to ensure that vibration
amplitudes which causes re-radiated noise do not exceed the limits detailed in
table 4 in section 7.7.2 of BS8233:2014 “Guidance on sound insulation and noise
reduction for buildings” or the plant shall be supported on adequate
proprietary anti-vibration mounts to reduce the structural transmission of
vibration and regenerated noise within adjoining premises. These shall be
so maintained thereafter. 























c)     A commissioning acoustic test and report shall be
undertaken within 30 Days of mechanical services commissioning to demonstrate
that conditions a) and b) above have been achieved. The results of the
test shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA.

External Lighting Prior to the installation of external
lighting, a lighting scheme shall be submitted to and approved in withing by
the Local Planning Authority. Such details shall include location, height, type
and direction of light sources and intensity of illumination. It shall also
detail implementation. Any lighting shall thereafter be installed prior to the
occupation of the relevant part of the development, or otherwise in compliance
with the implementation strategy. Any lighting so installed shall not
thereafter be altered without the prior consent in writing of the LPA other
than for routine maintenance which does not change its details. The scheme shall conform to
The Institution of Lighting Engineers ‘Guidance for the Reduction of Obtrusive
Light’ – Table 1 ‘Obtrusive Light Limitations for Exterior
Lighting Installations’.
description: Application for the approval of reserved matters pursuant to Conditions 38 and 39 following outline approval 18/00940/FUL for Plot 210A and 210B within Stage 2 South.
